Hi Acme / Jane,

Thanks — happy to clarify. Answers below are intended for the SIG sheet; I've attached the formal Incident Response Plan and a completed SIG tab for your review.

1) Notification trigger & timeline: Redwood's standard customer notification practice is to send an interim notification within 72 hours of confirming unauthorized access to customer data or systems. We do not send substantive notifications solely on initial detection unless confirmation is available; the 72-hour clock starts upon confirmation.

2) Contacts & escalation: primary IR contact is security@redwood.com (monitored 24/7). For faster response:
- Primary triage: Dev Patel, Site Reliability Lead (dev_patel@redwood.com)
- Legal/regulatory escalation: Hannah Schmitt, Counsel (hannah_schmitt@redwood.com)
- Executive/PR escalation (if needed): Evelyn Hart, Head of Communications (evelyn_hart@redwood.com)
Phone escalation (for critical incidents) is available via the security team pager — include security@redwood.com in the subject and we will initiate the on-call pager.

3) Regulatory notifications: we coordinate with affected customers on regulator notifications. Redwood does not unilaterally notify supervisory authorities on behalf of customers unless contractually required; we provide the evidence packet, timeline, and recommended notification language. For GDPR-related incidents we can assemble the data elements customers need to submit; timing depends on customer decisions but we aim to provide an evidence summary within the interim notification.

4) Post-incident deliverables: interim update within 24-72 hours after confirmation (status and scope), and a draft root-cause analysis (RCA) typically within 30 calendar days. If complexity requires more time we communicate expected delivery and milestones.

5) Evidence & templates: attached: incident_response_plan_v2.pdf and SIG_answers_Acme_20251110.xlsx. Also attached is a redacted sample customer notification template you can reuse.

If you want, we can set a short call to walk through the plan and contacts — I can loop Dev and Hannah.

Best,

Jane — good questions. Quick clarifications and next steps:

- 72-hour window: this is measured in calendar hours (includes weekends/holidays). The goal is to provide an interim notification as soon as possible; if an incident is confirmed on a Friday evening the 72-hour timeline still applies.

- RCA deliverables: we provide an interim customer-facing summary within the 72-hour window (scope, affected assets, immediate mitigations). The 30-day deliverable is typically a technical RCA draft (timeline, root cause, evidence, log extracts when shareable, and mitigations). We'll also prepare a concise customer-facing executive summary if you request it.

- Insurance certificate: Redwood maintains a cyber liability policy; we can provide an insurer's certificate upon request (redacted as needed). I'll loop our Legal and Finance teams to generate the cert.

Next steps / action items:
1) We'll upload the incident_response_plan_v2.pdf and SIG_answers sheet to the shared Drive link I sent.
